interaction.source: Illinois Statewide Technical Reference Manual v14.0 (effective January 1, 2026), Vol. 2, Section 4.5 reference table, Hotel/Motel - Guest and Hotel/Motel - Common (OpenStudio models based on Chicago): cooling saved = WHFe - 1 (1.17 and 1.09) kWh per kWh of lighting saved; heating added = IFTherms 0.020 and 0.017 therms per kWh (0.586 and 0.498 kBtu per kBtu, gas), resistance IFkWh 0.468 and 0.406, heat pump IFkWh 0.204 and 0.176. Applied in site energy to the heating and cooling cells. PTAC is treated as resistance heated (a PTHP would be closer to the heat-pump value).

upgrades.label: Smart guest-room thermostats and occupancy sensing
upgrades.description: Sets vacant and away rooms back and recovers when a guest returns.

comfort.note: Rooms need recovery time when a guest returns; check the recovery setting.

upgrades.source: Cost $260 per room and life 15 years: Illinois Statewide TRM v14.0, Vol. 2, measure 4.4.8 Guest Room Energy Management (read in the primary text), which also requires an unoccupied setback of at least 5 F; $100 and $500 bounds from the California 2013 CASE report (search excerpt). Setback 5 F mid; 3 F and 7 F are PLACEHOLDER bounds. Calibration check: IL-TRM 4.4.8 deems 92 to 147 kWh and 3.0 to 6.5 therms saved per ton of guest-room cooling for a Chicago hotel with central hot-water fan coils and gas heat (with or without housekeeping setback); see docs/08 for how the model compares.

upgrades.label: Roof and envelope insulation
upgrades.description: Cuts the weather-driven heating and cooling load.
upgrades.source: Weather-load reduction mid 10%: consistent with NREL ComStock roof insulation to ASHRAE AEDG levels (about 11% of gas heating and 12% of electric heating, stock-wide). Low and high: PLACEHOLDER. Cost: PLACEHOLDER $3.50 per ft2 of roof (contractor ranges $2 to $7 per ft2 for insulation only). Life: PLACEHOLDER. Scaling: the reduction applies to a building of up to 5 floors and is multiplied by 5 / floors above that, because roof insulation mainly affects the top floors (a modeling assumption, not a sourced value).

upgrades.label: LED lighting retrofit
upgrades.description: Replaces remaining non-LED lamps and fixtures throughout the hotel.
upgrades.source: Lighting reduction: low 27% (linear LED replacing fluorescent, PNNL evaluation for GSA, search excerpt), high 60% (incandescent-heavy fixtures); mid 45% is a judgment between them for a mixed hotel stock. Life: 12 years, from the IL-TRM v14.0 4.5.4 rule (rated life divided by operating hours, capped at 15 years): about 8 to 11 years at common-area hours (4,542 to 6,138 h a year, IL-TRM 4.5 reference table) and the 15-year cap in guest rooms (777 h). Cost: PLACEHOLDER $0.40/$0.60/$0.90 per ft2.

upgrades.label: Occupancy sensors in common areas and hallways
upgrades.description: Dims or turns off lighting and trims ventilation in unoccupied public areas.

comfort.note: A missed detection can leave a space dark; set sensible time delays.

upgrades.source: Lighting reduction in common areas and hallways: mid 24%, the energy savings factor for an interior occupancy sensor in the Illinois Statewide TRM v14.0 (effective January 1, 2026), Vol. 2, measure 4.5.10 (based on Williams et al., LBNL 2012); high 37%, the same with high-end trim; low 12% is a PLACEHOLDER (poorly set or partly bypassed controls). Life: 10 years (IL-TRM 4.5.10, lighting controls other than networked or luminaire-level). Cost: PLACEHOLDER $0.25/$0.40/$0.65 per ft2 of common area; the IL-TRM gives $55 to $125 incremental cost per sensor, but no coverage area to convert it. Ventilation reduction: PLACEHOLDER. Read in the primary TRM text.

upgrades.label: Energy management controls (scheduling and optimization)
upgrades.description: Schedules and tunes the central plant, public-area HVAC and fans.

comfort.note: Poorly set schedules can reduce comfort; commissioning matters.

upgrades.source: HVAC reduction 4/7/10%: consistent with a 3% whole-building median saving for lodging retro-commissioning (Crowe, Mills et al. 2020, Energy and Buildings, about 1,500 buildings), which is about 7.6% of HVAC energy if all of it is HVAC (39.5% HVAC share, CBECS 2018 lodging). Cost: PLACEHOLDER $15,000 + $0.20 per ft2; for comparison the retro-commissioning median is $0.26 per ft2 (Crowe 2020), without control hardware. Life: PLACEHOLDER. Values seen in search excerpts; to confirm.

upgrades.label: High-efficiency HVAC equipment
upgrades.description: Replaces the heating and cooling equipment with higher-efficiency units, sized from the reduced load.
upgrades.source: Heating reduction mid 13%: replacing an 80% efficient boiler (typical existing stock, GSA evaluation) with a condensing boiler at about 92% seasonal efficiency gives 1 - 0.80/0.92 = 13%; NREL ComStock (Condensing Gas Boilers, 2025) reports 9% site savings for an example building. Low and high, cooling reduction, cost and life: PLACEHOLDER. Values seen in search excerpts; to confirm. Boiler part, for reference: IL-TRM v14.0 4.4.10 High Efficiency Boiler gives a full installed cost of $22.95 per kBtu/h for a condensing hot-water boiler (over 90% combustion efficiency; $12.94 for 85 to 90%) and a 25-year life; at the model's boiler size (0.03 kBtu/h per ft2) that is about $38,000 for the demo hotel. The chiller cost is not sourced, so the combined $2.00 per ft2 stays a PLACEHOLDER.

upgrades.label: High-efficiency water heating and low-flow fixtures
upgrades.description: Condensing water heaters and low-flow fixtures.

comfort.note: Guests may notice lower flow at fixtures.

upgrades.source: PLACEHOLDER. Replace with ENERGY STAR and DOE hotel water-heating guidance.

upgrades.label: Rooftop solar (a quarter of the usable roof)
upgrades.description: Sized to 25% of the usable roof (never above the hotel's yearly electricity use). Output comes from the location's solar data; the hotel uses what it can hour by hour and any surplus is exported at the region's export credit. Yearly operation and maintenance is subtracted.
upgrades.source: Sizing: PLACEHOLDER usable roof share (0.5) and roof area per kW (100 ft2). Output: the climate's solar data (PVWatts). Cost: the region's installed cost per W (PLACEHOLDER). Operation and maintenance: $17.63 per kW (DC) a year for 2024 ($14.17 system plus $3.46 administration), NLR Annual Technology Baseline 2025, Commercial PV (atb.nlr.gov, read in the primary page). Degradation: 0.5% a year; Jordan et al. 2022, 'Photovoltaic fleet degradation insights', Progress in Photovoltaics (NREL/TP 81314): fleet median 0.75% a year, cooler climates 0.48% a year (read in the primary paper). Inverter replacement is not included.
